task: Branch Environments: per-branch schemas in the stage Warehouse, defer to stage, rebuild only changed Steps, drop on merge

analysis.objective: Add Branch Environments to adops: `adops run <pipeline> --branch <name>` runs a Pipeline in branch-prefixed schemas inside the stage Environment's Warehouse, rebuilding only the first Changed Step (by Step Fingerprint versus stage's last successful run) and every later Step, and deferring to stage's tables for the unchanged earlier Steps; a new CLI command drops every schema with that branch's prefix. Both work on Postgres and DuckDB Warehouses and are proven in the Docker demo E2E. This is horizon 6's slice of vision success criterion (5), without the CI automation.
analysis.successDefinition: Done when ALL hold. (1) A successful stage run of a Step, after all its Checks pass, saves that Step's Step Fingerprint in the stage Warehouse's adops schema. The fingerprint is a deterministic hash of the Step's YAML definition plus the files it depends on (for a Transform Step, the dbt project files, excluding generated target/, logs/ and .adops/). Running the same files on another machine or another day gives the same hash. dev runs and Branch Environment runs never write stage fingerprints. (2) `adops run <pipeline> --branch <name>` derives a Branch Environment from the stage Environment's settings: same Warehouse, Sources and targets. It names it br_<sanitized name> and uses schemas br_<name>__raw_<source>, br_<name>__analytics and br_<name>__adops. It computes fingerprints for every Step. The first Step whose fingerprint differs from stage's, or that stage has none for, and every later Step run in branch schemas. Earlier Steps do not run, and the Steps that do run read stage's raw_<source>/analytics tables for them. A Transform Step after an unchanged Sync Step reads stage's raw_<source>. A Reverse Sync Step reads the branch's analytics when the Transform was rebuilt, and stage's otherwise. (3) A branch run re-syncs Sources only when a Sync Step, or a Step before it, changed. (4) A branch run where nothing changed runs no Step, exits 0 and says it uses stage. A branch run with no stage fingerprints for the Pipeline fails with a clear, sanitized error asking you to run stage first. --branch without a stage Environment in adops.yaml fails clearly. (5) Every Reverse Sync in a Branch Environment yields a Preview and never writes, enforced by the existing exact stage/prod name rule. (6) The drop command removes every Warehouse schema with prefix br_<name>__ (CASCADE) and the local dlt state folder <project>/.adops/dlt/<branch env>. It never touches a schema without that exact prefix, uses quoted identifiers, and succeeds idempotently when nothing exists. (7) Stage tables, fingerprints and snapshots are byte-for-byte unchanged by any branch run or drop. (8) The Docker demo E2E, on both Postgres and DuckDB Warehouses: runs stage; changes only the dbt model and shows the branch rebuilds only Transform + Reverse Sync with no re-sync; changes the Sync Step and shows a re-sync into br_ schemas; shows a no-change branch run; drops the branch and asserts the br_ schemas are gone and stage's remain. The whole E2E finishes inside the unchanged 20-minute CI job. (9) The repo gates hold: 100% line+branch coverage with no new pragma; domain/application purity rules; no secret value in any output, log or error (asserted by tests); `uv sync --locked`; wheel template check. (10) ADR-0006's schema wording is clarified by a recorded decision (env_<branch> → per-kind br_<branch>__<schema>), and GLOSSARY gains the new terms.
assumptions: The CLI flag is `--branch <name>` on `adops run`. The drop command is assumed to be `adops drop-branch <name>`, with the exact verb fixed at planning. Using --branch together with --env is a usage error, because a Branch Environment always derives from stage.

Branch name sanitization: lowercase it, turn every non-[a-z0-9] run into '_', trim leading and trailing '_', and add the br_ prefix. Cap the length so the longest generated schema (br_<name>__raw_<longest source>) fits Postgres' 63-byte identifier limit. When truncation happens, add a short hash suffix so two long branch names cannot collide. An empty result after sanitizing is a usage error.
Because of the br_ prefix, a Branch Environment's name can never equal stage or prod, so the horizon-5 decision 'only stage/prod write' automatically makes every branch Reverse Sync a Preview.
Branch Environments are not declared in adops.yaml. They exist only as a CLI argument plus their Warehouse schemas and local dlt state.

Step Fingerprints live in a new table in the stage Warehouse's adops schema (alongside _adops_schema_snapshots), keyed by pipeline + Step name. They are saved per Step only after all that Step's Checks pass, matching the snapshot decision.

What goes into a fingerprint: Sync Step = its YAML definition (source, tables, modes, checks, skip reasons). Transform Step = its YAML plus dbt_project.yml, models/, macros/, tests/, seeds/ and sources yml, hashed in sorted path order with normalized line endings. Reverse Sync Step = its YAML definition. The Environment settings are not hashed, because the branch reuses stage's settings by construction.
A Step that is new, renamed or reordered relative to stage's fingerprints counts as changed. Because Steps are linear (horizon-2 decision), 'dependents' means every later Step.

How deferral reaches dbt: adops tells the dbt Transform which schemas to read raw_<source> from and write analytics to (for example through dbt vars or a schema override it controls). Demo and plain templates may change so sources.yml schemas are parameterized. The user's dbt project keeps working unchanged for dev/stage/prod.

A branch's Breaking Change baseline is its own br_<name>__adops snapshot schema. A branch's first re-sync takes a fresh baseline, as a new Environment does today. Its dlt state starts empty, so Incremental Steps do a full load in the branch.
Branch runs and drops are sequential, one process at a time. On DuckDB the branch schemas live in the stage DuckDB file.
The demo E2E switches the demo to its stage Environment, which already exists since horizon 5, to run stage, then branch, then drop, for both Warehouse kinds in one compose stack.

risks: The dbt Source schema is hard-coded in the demo sources.yml (raw_shop) and dbt writes to a constant TARGET_SCHEMA 'analytics'. Making dbt read stage's raw schema while writing br_<name>__analytics needs a schema-override mechanism. That could change user-facing dbt project files and must keep dev/stage/prod behaviour identical.

Schema names are module constants in several adapters: the dlt dataset raw_<source>, dbt analytics, the snapshot schema adops, and the Reverse Sync reader. Threading a per-run schema prefix through DltSync, WarehouseSnapshotStore, DbtTransform and PostgresReverseSync touches every adapter and their 100%-covered tests.

An unstable fingerprint makes every branch rebuild everything, silently defeating 'rebuild only changed Steps'. Causes include CRLF line endings, file order, dbt target/ or logs/ artifacts, .pyc files, and YAML key order or comments. A fingerprint that misses a real dependency (for example a macro or packages.yml) makes the branch wrongly defer to stale stage tables.

Stage fingerprints are saved per Step. If a stage run fails after an earlier Step succeeded, stage tables and fingerprints must still agree. Saving a fingerprint before the Step's Checks pass would let a branch defer to a broken stage table.

The drop command is destructive. A sanitization or prefix-matching bug (for example a LIKE pattern where '_' is a wildcard, or a missing trailing '__') could drop stage schemas such as raw_shop or analytics. Matching must be exact and the identifiers quoted.
Two branch names that collide after sanitization or truncation would share or drop each other's schemas unless a hash suffix makes truncated names distinct.

DuckDB: dbt-duckdb keeps a process-wide handle open and the file is single-writer. Reading stage schemas while writing branch schemas in one file within one process, and dropping schemas from another process while one is open, could hit locks.

A Reverse Sync in a branch reads stage's targets (operational DBs) to compute the Preview Diff. It must never write, and that rests entirely on the exact-name rule. Any code path that passes the base Environment name 'stage' instead of the branch name would cause real writes.

Change detection compares against the stage Warehouse, not Git. If stage was last run from a different commit than the branch's base, the branch rebuilds Steps it did not itself change. This is accepted by the user's choice but may surprise.

E2E time: adding stage + branch + drop scenarios on two Warehouse kinds on top of the current ~110s run should still fit 20 minutes. The known flaky '999'-in-Dagster-UUID assertion could surface more often with more runs.

Conflict with the vision wording: criterion (5) says 'dropped on merge/close', but the user scoped automatic triggering on PR merge/close to a later horizon. This horizon delivers only the manual drop command, so criterion (5) stays partially open until the GitHub Actions horizon.

Conflict with ADR-0006's wording 'its own schema (e.g. env_add_refunds)': the confirmed layout is several per-kind schemas with a br_<branch>__ prefix. This must be recorded as a clarifying decision, not left as a silent contradiction.
outOfScope: Generating GitHub Actions workflows (PR opened → Branch Environment run, PR merged/closed → drop): the user deferred CI automation to a later horizon. This horizon proves the CLI commands only.
dbt model-level --defer/--state (rebuilding only the modified dbt models inside a Transform Step): explicitly out of scope by the user. The Transform Step is the unit of change.
Git-based change detection (diffing against a base branch or commit): the user chose fingerprint comparison with stage's last run, and no Git is used.
Declaring Branch Environments in adops.yaml or letting them override Warehouse, Sources or targets: Branch Environments are derived from stage settings only.
MCP server and Assistant skills operating Branch Environments: those interfaces are not built yet and belong to the Assistant horizons.
Keeping secrets away from forked-PR workflows: there are no generated workflows in this horizon (open blocker deferred with CI).
Automatic cleanup of stale or abandoned branch schemas (TTL, listing orphaned br_ schemas): only an explicit drop by branch name is in scope.
Running several Branch Environments concurrently with locking or isolation guarantees: runs are assumed to be sequential, especially on single-writer DuckDB.
Deferring Branch Environments to prod or to dev, or chaining branches off other branches: ADR-0006 fixes stage as the base.

Seeding a branch's Breaking Change baseline from stage's snapshots: a branch re-sync takes a fresh baseline like any new Environment. Cross-Environment snapshot comparison is a separate design question.
Step graphs or partial downstream rebuilds: Steps stay linear (horizon-2 decision), so every later Step is rebuilt.
Promotion (Branch → stage → prod via Git) and the Environments/Promotion playbook: these are separate vision criteria for later horizons.
adops accept-schema --branch: user chose to record it as a known gap; a branch takes a fresh baseline on its first re-sync, so it is rare
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective encodes DataOps rules a data engineer recognizes: a Branch Environment defers to stage, only changed Steps and their dependents rebuild, re-sync only on Sync change, branches never write via Reverse Sync, and branches are disposable. It sits within the existing Environment/Pipeline bounded contexts, even though it touches Warehouse schema machinery.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: A disposable Environment for one Git branch, derived from the stage Environment's settings and living as br_<branch>__-prefixed schemas in the stage Warehouse.
The Environment named exactly stage, whose Warehouse hosts the Branch schemas and whose last successful run is the baseline a Branch Environment defers to.
A deterministic hash of a Step's YAML definition and the files it depends on, saved per Step after a successful stage run and recomputed by every branch run.
A Step whose Step Fingerprint differs from, or is missing in, stage's record; it and every later Step are rebuilt in the Branch Environment.
A Branch Environment reading stage's tables for unchanged earlier Steps instead of running them.
A Warehouse schema named br_<branch>__<kind> (raw_<source>, analytics, adops) that belongs to exactly one Branch Environment.
Removing every Branch Schema with a branch's exact prefix plus its local dlt state, leaving stage untouched.
The non-writing Reverse Sync report every Branch Environment gets, because only Environments named exactly stage or prod write.

phases.name: Add Branch Environment rules to the domain
phases.goal: Create one pure domain module that holds every Branch Environment rule: turning a Git branch name into a safe Branch Environment name, naming its Branch Schemas, computing a Step Fingerprint, finding the first Changed Step, and deciding when a fingerprint may be saved.
phases.rationale: A Branch Environment is a throwaway copy of the stage Environment for one Git branch. It lives as extra schemas in the stage Warehouse (the database that holds synced and transformed tables). Every later phase (the run use case, the adapters, the drop command) depends on the same naming and change-detection rules. Keeping those rules pure, with no file or database access, makes them deterministic and fully unit-testable. It also keeps them inside the repo's domain-purity rules.
changes: Add src/adops/domain/branch_environment.py. Add `branch_environment_name(branch: str, longest_source: str) -> str`: lowercase the name, turn every run of characters outside [a-z0-9] into '_', trim leading and trailing '_', then add the 'br_' prefix. Cap the length so the longest generated schema, br_<name>__raw_<longest_source>_staging, fits Postgres' 63-byte identifier limit. (dlt, the loading library, creates a '<schema>_staging' companion for merge and incremental loads.) When the name is cut short, end it with a short hashlib sha256 suffix so two long branch names cannot collide. The result must match names.IDENTIFIER. Raise PipelineValidationError with a plain usage message when nothing is left after sanitizing.

Add a frozen `SchemaLayout` value with `raw(source)`, `analytics` and `adops` schema names. `SchemaLayout.default()` returns today's names (raw_<source>, analytics, adops), so dev and stage stay byte-identical; `SchemaLayout.for_branch(env_name)` returns br_<name>__raw_<source>, br_<name>__analytics and br_<name>__adops. The domain only names schemas: it carries no loader-library flag (the adapters handle dlt's name normalization themselves).

Add `read_layout(branch_layout, first_changed_index, steps)`. It answers, for every Step that runs in the branch, which raw_<source> schema to read (stage's when that source's Sync Step was deferred, the branch's when it was rebuilt) and which analytics schema a Reverse Sync Step reads (the branch's when the Transform Step was rebuilt, stage's otherwise).

Add `step_fingerprint(step_json: str, files: Mapping[str, bytes]) -> str`. It returns a sha256 hash over the canonical Step JSON (json.dumps(sort_keys=True) of model_dump(mode='json')) followed by each file, in sorted POSIX-path order, with CRLF normalized to LF.

Add `first_changed_step(current: Sequence[tuple[str, str]], stage: Mapping[str, str]) -> int | None`. It returns the index of the first Step whose fingerprint differs from stage's or is missing from it, so new, renamed and reordered Steps count as changed. It returns None when nothing changed.
Add `saves_stage_fingerprint(environment_name: str) -> bool`, which is True only for exactly 'stage', and `drop_prefix(env_name) -> str`, which returns '<env_name>__'.

Add `uses_raw_schema_var(files: Mapping[str, bytes], source: str) -> bool`, True when some dbt .yml file in the Transform's project references the variable adops_raw_schema_<source>. It lets a branch run refuse to build analytics from stage's old raw tables when a rebuilt Sync's raw schema is not reachable from the user's dbt sources.

Add tests/unit/domain/test_branch_environment.py covering every line and branch: sanitizing edge cases, truncation with the hash suffix, two distinct long names producing distinct results, empty input, stable hashes across file order and CRLF, and the missing, renamed and new Step cases.

rubric.label: Branch names always yield valid, collision-safe schema names
rubric.ruleStatement: branch_environment_name turns any Git branch name into a br_-prefixed name such that every schema it generates, including the longest br_<name>__raw_<longest_source>_staging, matches names.IDENTIFIER and fits Postgres' 63-byte limit, and two distinct long branch names never map to the same name. 10 = property-style or table-driven tests over slashes, unicode, dots, leading/trailing separators and >63-byte inputs, all asserting the full staging schema length; 8 = competent explicit cases for each; minScore is acceptable, not perfect.
passCriteria: Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/domain/test_branch_environment.py -q`: it passes.
In a Python shell, `branch_environment_name('feature/ABC-12.fix', 'shop')` returns a value starting with 'br_' that contains only [a-z0-9_] and matches `adops.domain.names.IDENTIFIER`.
For a 200-character branch name and a 30-character source, the returned name n satisfies `len(f'{n}__raw_{source}_staging'.encode()) <= 63`.
Two 200-character branch names that differ only in their last character return different names (hash suffix present).
`branch_environment_name('///', 'shop')` raises PipelineValidationError with a message that tells the user the branch name is unusable.
failureExamples: Truncation caps br_<name> at 63 bytes but forgets the '__raw_<source>_staging' suffix, so dlt's staging schema is silently truncated by Postgres.
Truncation keeps a prefix only, so 'feature/very-long-name-a' and 'feature/very-long-name-b' collide and one branch drops the other's schemas.
A trailing '_' left after truncation produces 'br_x___raw_shop', breaking the exact '__' drop prefix.

rubric.label: Step Fingerprint is stable across irrelevant differences and sensitive to real ones
rubric.ruleStatement: step_fingerprint returns the same hash regardless of Mapping insertion order and CRLF vs LF line endings, and a different hash when the Step JSON, any file's content, or any file's path changes. 10 = also proves a renamed file with identical bytes changes the hash and that path/content boundaries cannot be shifted to forge equal hashes; 8 = order, CRLF, content and Step-JSON cases tested.
passCriteria: In test_branch_environment.py there is a test that passes the same files in two different dict orders and asserts equal fingerprints.
There is a test where one file uses '\r\n' and the other '\n' with otherwise equal text, asserting equal fingerprints.
There are tests asserting a changed byte in one file, a renamed file path, and a changed Step JSON field each yield a different fingerprint.
`grep -n 'sort_keys' src/adops/domain/branch_environment.py` or the call site shows Step JSON is canonicalized before hashing.
failureExamples: Files are concatenated without a path or length separator, so moving bytes from the end of a.sql to the start of b.sql gives the same hash.
Only file contents are hashed, so renaming models/customer_stats.sql to another path does not count as a change.
CRLF normalization is applied to the Step JSON but not to the files, so a Windows checkout rebuilds everything.

rubric.label: First Changed Step handles new, missing, renamed and reordered Steps
rubric.ruleStatement: first_changed_step returns the index of the earliest Step whose fingerprint differs from or is absent in stage's mapping, and None only when every current Step matches stage. 10 = adds a case where stage holds extra Steps the branch removed and documents the chosen behaviour in a test name; 8 = each listed case tested.
passCriteria: Tests assert: identical mappings -> None; second Step changed -> 1; a Step name not in stage -> its index; two Steps swapped in order with unchanged content -> index of the first moved Step; empty stage mapping -> 0.

`read_layout` tests assert that for first_changed_index 0 every raw schema is the branch's, and for an index after the Sync Step the raw schema is stage's raw_<source> while analytics is the branch's.
`saves_stage_fingerprint('stage')` is True and `saves_stage_fingerprint('Stage')`, `('br_stage')`, `('prod')` and `('dev')` are False in tests.
failureExamples: Comparison is by set of fingerprints, so swapping two Steps' order returns None and the branch defers to stage tables built in a different order.
A Step present in the branch but absent from stage is skipped instead of counted as changed.
saves_stage_fingerprint uses `startswith('stage')` or case-insensitive compare, letting 'stage_test' overwrite stage's baseline.

rubric.label: Domain module names schemas without adapter or loader knowledge
rubric.ruleStatement: branch_environment.py expresses only Branch Environment rules: it holds no SQL text, no dlt normalization flag or dataset-option, no filesystem walk and no knowledge of dbt's generated folders. 10 = SchemaLayout is a frozen value whose only behaviour is naming; 8 = no adapter concept leaks though helpers may be loosely grouped. The purity test already proves imports; this dimension checks concepts.
passCriteria: `grep -nEi 'enable_dataset_name_normalization|DROP SCHEMA|CREATE |information_schema|target/|dbt_packages|duckdb|postgres' src/adops/domain/branch_environment.py` prints nothing (comments explaining the 63-byte Postgres limit excepted).
`SchemaLayout` is declared frozen (pydantic frozen config or `@dataclass(frozen=True)`) and assigning to an attribute in a test raises.
`SchemaLayout.default().raw('shop') == 'raw_shop'`, `.analytics == 'analytics'`, `.adops == 'adops'`, so dev and stage are byte-identical.
failureExamples: SchemaLayout exposes a `dlt_normalize: bool` field because the author knew adapters would need it.
uses_raw_schema_var filters out target/ and logs/ paths itself, duplicating the infrastructure exclusion list.
SchemaLayout.default() returns 'raw__shop' due to a shared format string, silently moving dev and stage tables.

phases.healerHint: The likely miss is computing the length cap for br_<name> alone instead of the full br_<name>__raw_<longest_source>_staging schema or leaving a trailing '_' after truncation; fix by computing the budget from the longest generated schema and stripping '_' before appending the hash suffix.

phases.name: Add deferral and Step Fingerprint saving to runs
phases.goal: Teach the Pipeline run use case to (a) save each Step's Step Fingerprint after a stage run's Checks pass and (b) in a Branch Environment, skip the unchanged earlier Steps and report them as deferred to stage.
phases.rationale: run_pipeline in the application layer builds and runs the list of Steps (Sync, Transform, Reverse Sync). It is the one place that knows when a Step has fully succeeded. Fingerprints must be saved only after Checks pass, so a branch never defers to a broken stage table. This phase adds the ports (interfaces the application calls; infrastructure implements them) without any real adapter, so the logic is proven against fakes first.
changes: In ports.py, add a `StepFingerprintStore` Protocol with `load(pipeline) -> Mapping[str, str]` and `save(pipeline, step, fingerprint) -> None`. Add a `ProjectFiles` Protocol with `read_tree(relative_dir) -> Mapping[str, bytes]`. Add `StepStatus.DEFERRED`, and let `RunResult.succeeded` accept PASSED or DEFERRED.

In run_pipeline.py, add a `BranchRun` input: the branch env name, the stage fingerprints and the first Changed Step index. Add one shared `current_fingerprints(steps, project_files)` that computes every Step's fingerprint through ProjectFiles and the domain `step_fingerprint` (Transform Steps hash their dbt project tree); stage runs and branch runs both use it, so the saved and compared hashes always come from the same inputs. Add `plan_branch_run(...)`, which calls current_fingerprints, loads stage's fingerprints, and calls `first_changed_step`. Raise a new `StageNotRunError` with the message 'run the Pipeline in stage first' when stage has no fingerprints for the Pipeline.

Wrap every StepTask, binding the store and the Step's value from current_fingerprints by closure, so it saves that fingerprint only when the inner task returns normally and `saves_stage_fingerprint(environment)` is True. dev and branch runs never save one.

Leave deferred Steps out of the RunPlan and add a synthetic DEFERRED StepReport for each. When nothing changed, return a RunResult without calling the Orchestrator (the component that executes the plan, e.g. Dagster).

Pass the branch env name, never 'stage', as the environment of PlannedReverseSyncStep, so writes_allowed keeps every branch Reverse Sync a Preview. Look up settings through pick_environment(…, 'stage') and raise a dedicated PipelineValidationError when adops.yaml has no stage Environment.

When a branch rebuilds a Sync Step for a source and a later Transform Step runs, check `uses_raw_schema_var` on that Transform's project files; if it is False, fail before any Step runs with a new BranchSourcesNotParameterizedError naming the source and the variable adops_raw_schema_<source> to use in dbt sources, instead of quietly reading stage's raw tables.

rubric.label: Stage fingerprints are saved only after a Step and its Checks succeed
rubric.ruleStatement: A Step Fingerprint is written to the StepFingerprintStore only when the environment is exactly 'stage' and that Step's task, including its Checks, returned normally; a failed Check, a raised error, a dev run or a branch run writes nothing. 10 = a test proves that when Step 2's Check fails, Step 1's fingerprint is saved and Step 2's and Step 3's are not; 8 = each condition tested separately.
passCriteria: Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/application/test_run_pipeline.py -q`: it passes.
A test runs a stage Pipeline whose Transform Check fails and asserts the fake store's saved keys contain the Sync Step only.
Tests run the same Pipeline with environment 'dev' and with a 'br_feat' environment and assert the fake store's save() was never called.
A test asserts the value saved in stage equals the value plan_branch_run compares for the same Step (both from current_fingerprints).
failureExamples: The fingerprint is saved before Checks run (at the end of the materialize call), so a branch later defers to a stage table that failed its Checks.
Save happens after the whole RunResult succeeds, so a later Step's failure prevents saving earlier, valid fingerprints and every branch rebuilds from Step 0.
Stage save hashes the Transform's dbt project tree but the branch compare hashes only the Step JSON, so every branch run sees a change.

rubric.label: Unchanged earlier Steps are DEFERRED and a no-change run never calls the Orchestrator
rubric.ruleStatement: In a branch run, Steps before the first Changed Step are absent from the RunPlan and reported as StepStatus.DEFERRED; the Changed Step and every later Step run; when nothing changed the result succeeds without invoking the Orchestrator. 10 = tests also assert report order matches Step order and RunResult.succeeded with a mix of DEFERRED and PASSED; 8 = each behaviour tested.

A test with an adops.yaml lacking a stage Environment asserts a PipelineValidationError naming the missing stage Environment.
failureExamples: Deferred Steps are kept in the RunPlan with a skip flag, so the Orchestrator still opens a Warehouse connection for them.
Only the Changed Step runs and later dependent Steps are deferred, so the Reverse Sync previews stale analytics.
RunResult.succeeded still checks `== PASSED`, so a branch run with deferred Steps exits non-zero.

rubric.label: A branch Reverse Sync is always a Preview
rubric.ruleStatement: Every PlannedReverseSyncStep built for a branch run carries the br_ environment name, never 'stage', so writes_allowed is False and apply() is never called. 10 = a test asserts this even when the stage Environment's settings enable writing; 8 = a test asserts the br_ environment and no apply call.

rubric.label: Rebuilt Sync with un-parameterized dbt sources fails before any Step runs
rubric.ruleStatement: When a branch rebuilds a Sync Step for a source and a later Transform's dbt project does not reference adops_raw_schema_<source>, the run raises BranchSourcesNotParameterizedError naming the source and the variable, before the Orchestrator runs anything. 10 = the message tells the user the exact var() expression to put in sources.yml; 8 = error raised with source and variable named.

rubric.ruleStatement: run_pipeline.py and ports.py read dbt project files only via ProjectFiles and fingerprints only via StepFingerprintStore, and never build schema strings, SQL, or file paths themselves. 10 = schema choices come solely from the domain read_layout/SchemaLayout; 8 = no adapter concept in application code.

phases.name: Write branch schemas and Step Fingerprints to Warehouse
phases.goal: Let the adapters that write to the Warehouse (dlt Sync and the schema snapshot store) take their schema names from a SchemaLayout instead of module constants, keeping '__' intact in branch schemas, and implement the StepFingerprintStore and ProjectFiles ports: Step Fingerprints live in a new _adops_step_fingerprints table in the stage Warehouse's adops schema, and the dbt project tree is read from disk minus generated folders. The default layout keeps dev and stage byte-identical.
phases.rationale: Today raw_<source> and adops are hard-coded constants in DltSync and WarehouseSnapshotStore, so a branch cannot write to br_<name>__ schemas. These are the write side of the Warehouse: their risk is dlt's dataset-name normalization collapsing '__' (including the *_staging companion dlt creates for merge and incremental loads). The Step Fingerprint store is another adops-schema writer that copies WarehouseSnapshotStore's dlt client pattern, so it belongs with it. Branch runs compare against stage's last successful run, so stage must persist one fingerprint per Pipeline and Step in the Warehouse both runs share, and file reading for fingerprints must skip dbt's generated target/, logs/, dbt_packages/, .adops/ and .pyc files, or every branch rebuilds everything.
changes: In dlt_sync.py, give DltSync a `layout: SchemaLayout = SchemaLayout.default()` keyword. Use layout.raw(step.source) as dataset_name. Whenever the schema name differs from the default one, build the dlt.destinations.postgres/duckdb factory with enable_dataset_name_normalization=False (dlt otherwise collapses '__' into '_'); pass nothing new in the default case.

In schema_snapshot_store.py, give WarehouseSnapshotStore a `layout` keyword and use layout.adops instead of SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA, disabling dlt dataset-name normalization when the schema is not the default.

Add src/adops/infrastructure/step_fingerprint_store.py with WarehouseFingerprintStore(project, warehouse_kind, environment). Copy WarehouseSnapshotStore._client's pattern: a dlt pipeline named 'adops_step_fingerprints' in local_state_dir(project, environment) with dataset 'adops'. Only save() creates the dataset if it is missing and runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _adops_step_fingerprints(pipeline, step, fingerprint, primary key pipeline+step), then upserts with parameterized SQL. load() first checks information_schema for the schema and table and returns {} when either is absent, without running any DDL, so a branch run never mutates the stage Warehouse's adops schema. Open DuckDB read-write only.

In the same module, add `read_project_tree(project_root, relative_dir) -> Mapping[str, bytes]`. It walks the directory and returns POSIX relative paths, excluding target/, logs/, dbt_packages/, .adops/ and *.pyc, and satisfies the ProjectFiles port.
Map driver failures to the existing WarehouseUnreachable so no DSN or driver text leaks.

phases.name: Add --branch option to adops run
phases.goal: `adops run <pipeline> --branch <name>` builds a Branch Environment from the stage Environment's settings, wires the adapters to the right schemas, prints deferred Steps as 'deferred to stage', and exits 0 when nothing changed.
phases.rationale: The CLI is where user input becomes adapter wiring. The branch name and the stage settings must become a br_ Environment name, a SchemaLayout and dlt state under .adops/dlt/br_<name>. Using --env together with --branch has to be rejected, because a Branch Environment always derives from stage. Stage runs also need the fingerprint store wired in, so they start saving fingerprints.
changes: Change run()'s --env default to None (meaning 'dev' when absent) and add a `--branch` option. Fail with a usage error when both are given.

Add build_fingerprint_store(project, kind) and build_project_files(project) as new module-level builders. Add branch layout arguments as defaulted keywords on build_sync, build_snapshot_store, build_transform and build_reverse_sync, so existing exact-signature monkeypatches in tests keep working.

In run_project, when --branch is given: read stage settings, compute the br_ name with branch_environment_name, call plan_branch_run, build the adapters with SchemaLayout.for_branch plus the read layout (stage raw or analytics for deferred Steps), and pass the br_ name as the environment. Always pass the fingerprint store so stage runs save fingerprints.

Print DEFERRED Steps as 'step <name>: deferred to stage'. On a run with no changes, print that the branch uses stage. Map StageNotRunError and a missing stage Environment to fail() with their plain messages.

Extend tests/unit/interface/test_run_command.py with CliRunner cases: --branch with --env is a usage error, a branch run wires br_ layouts and env name, no-change output and exit 0, stage-not-run error, no stage Environment error, and a stage run passes a fingerprint store. Assert no secret value appears in the output.
inputs: DltSync/WarehouseSnapshotStore SchemaLayout keywords, WarehouseFingerprintStore and read_project_tree from phase 2
DbtTransform and PostgresReverseSync schema keywords from phase 3
phases.expectedResult: `adops run <pipeline> --branch <name>` in src/adops/interface/run_command.py runs a Branch Environment end-to-end against fakes and adapters, covered by tests/unit/interface/test_run_command.py at 100%.
guardNotes: g3: every new CLI branch has a CliRunner test in test_run_command.py.
g7: unexpected errors still print only their type. The new error messages carry no DSN, and the tests assert the secret is absent. Adapters reach Dagster ops only by closure.

rubric.label: --branch wires every adapter to the right schemas and env name
rubric.ruleStatement: `adops run <pipeline> --branch <name>` builds Sync, snapshot store, Transform and Reverse Sync with SchemaLayout.for_branch for rebuilt Steps, the stage raw/analytics schemas for deferred inputs, dlt state under .adops/dlt/br_<name>, and the br_ name as environment, using stage's Warehouse settings. 10 = a test asserts every builder's received layout/schema arguments for both a Transform-only change and a Sync change; 8 = one branch scenario asserts all four builders.
passCriteria: Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/interface/test_run_command.py -q`: it passes.

A CliRunner test with monkeypatched builders runs `run shop_sync --branch feat` and asserts build_transform received target schema 'br_feat__analytics', build_reverse_sync received environment starting 'br_feat', and the Warehouse connection came from the stage Environment.
A test with only the Transform changed asserts build_transform received raw_schemas mapping shop to 'raw_shop' (stage's), not 'br_feat__raw_shop'.
Existing test monkeypatches of build_sync/build_transform with their previous signatures still pass unchanged.
failureExamples: The branch run uses dev's Warehouse settings because the env default stayed 'dev' instead of resolving stage.
dlt state is written under .adops/dlt/stage, so a branch Sync advances stage's incremental cursor.
Layout keywords are added as required positional arguments, breaking existing monkeypatched builders.

rubric.label: Conflicting options and missing baselines fail with plain usage messages
rubric.ruleStatement: Passing --env with --branch is a usage error; a missing stage run or stage Environment exits non-zero with its plain message; deferred Steps print 'step <name>: deferred to stage' and a no-change run says the branch uses stage and exits 0. 10 = exit codes and exact output lines asserted for all four cases; 8 = each case asserted with substring checks.
passCriteria: `adops run shop_sync --env stage --branch feat` (CliRunner) exits with a non-zero usage code and mentions both options.
A no-change branch run exits 0 and its output contains 'deferred to stage' for each Step plus a line saying the branch uses stage.
With an empty fingerprint store the output contains 'run the Pipeline in stage first' and the exit code is non-zero.
`adops run shop_sync` with no flags still runs dev (existing tests unchanged).
failureExamples: --env keeps default 'dev', so `--branch` alone is indistinguishable from `--env dev --branch` and the conflict check fires always or never.
StageNotRunError falls into the generic except and prints only 'StageNotRunError' with no guidance.

rubric.label: Plain stage runs get the fingerprint store wired in
rubric.ruleStatement: `adops run <pipeline> --env stage` passes a WarehouseFingerprintStore and project-files reader into run_pipeline, so stage begins recording baselines; dev runs pass a store too but the use case never saves for them. 10 = a test asserts the store's kind and environment arguments match stage's Warehouse; 8 = a test asserts a store is passed for stage.
passCriteria: A CliRunner test monkeypatches build_fingerprint_store and asserts it was called with the stage Environment's warehouse kind for `--env stage`.
A test asserts run_pipeline receives a non-None fingerprint store and project files for a stage run.
failureExamples: The store is only built inside the `if branch:` path, so stage never saves fingerprints and every later branch hits StageNotRunError.

rubric.label: No secret value appears in any branch run output
rubric.ruleStatement: For every new path (branch success, no-change, stage-not-run, missing stage, usage error, unexpected adapter error) the CLI output contains no resolved Warehouse secret. 10 = a single parametrized test sets a distinctive secret env var and asserts it is absent across all paths; 8 = asserted on the error paths.
passCriteria: A test sets the stage Warehouse secret env var to a distinctive value (e.g. 'S3cr3t-xyz') and, for each new CliRunner case, asserts that value is not in `result.output`.
A test where a builder raises an exception whose message contains the secret asserts only the exception type is printed.
failureExamples: The branch summary prints the resolved stage connection to show which Warehouse is used.
The secret check is done only on the happy path; the unexpected-error path echoes str(exc).

phases.healerHint: The likely failure is the branch run reusing dev settings or stage's dlt state dir because --env still defaults to 'dev'; fix by defaulting --env to None, resolving stage settings explicitly for --branch, and passing local_state_dir(project, br_name) to the Sync builder.

phases.name: Add adops command to drop a branch
phases.goal: `adops drop-branch <name>` removes every stage-Warehouse schema whose name starts with exactly br_<name>__ (including dlt's *_staging schemas), using DROP SCHEMA "…" CASCADE, and deletes only the local dlt state folder .adops/dlt/br_<name>. It succeeds when nothing exists.
phases.rationale: This is one small slice across layers: a use case, one adapter and one CLI command, roughly 200 lines in under 10 files, and no other phase consumes any of it. The drop is destructive, so the prefix match must be an exact Python startswith on the sanitized name with a trailing '__' (never a SQL LIKE, where '_' is a wildcard) and quoted identifiers, so stage schemas such as raw_shop and analytics can never match.
changes: Add src/adops/application/drop_branch.py: drop_branch(settings_text, branch, env, schemas, state) resolves only the stage Environment's Warehouse secret with resolve_warehouse, computes the br_ name and drop_prefix from the domain, lists schemas, drops those starting with the prefix, then deletes the local state. A small WarehouseSchemas Protocol (list_schemas, drop) is declared next to the use case.

Add src/adops/infrastructure/warehouse_schemas.py: it lists schemas from information_schema.schemata and drops with DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS "<name>" CASCADE through warehouse_client, opening DuckDB read-write. Add a function that removes local_state_dir(project, br_name) only when it exists, never .adops/ or the DuckDB file.
Add src/adops/interface/drop_branch_command.py (def drop_branch) with accept_schema_command's except ladder, so no driver text leaks. Register it in cli.py as 'drop-branch'.

Add tests: application tests with fakes (only prefixed schemas dropped, raw_shop/analytics/br_other__ untouched, idempotent when none exist), infrastructure tests on DuckDB and the CI Postgres service (including a *_staging schema and a locked DuckDB file), and CliRunner tests asserting no secret appears in the output.
phases.expectedResult: `adops drop-branch <name>` drops exactly the br_<name>__ schemas and the branch's local dlt state, idempotently, covered at 100% by its three unit test files.
guardNotes: g3: the use case, adapter and command each have a test file. Postgres-backed tests run against the CI service.
g6: drop_branch.py imports no dlt or typer. The schema access sits behind the WarehouseSchemas Protocol.
g10: application/drop_branch.py uses no os or pathlib. Folder deletion lives in infrastructure.
g7: no pragma. Errors map to plain messages with no DSN or driver text, and the tests assert it.
phases.compensation: A drop cannot be undone, but it only ever touches br_<name>__ schemas and .adops/dlt/br_<name>. Recover by re-running `adops run <pipeline> --branch <name>`. Stage data is never at risk, because the prefix match is exact and tested against stage schema names.

rubric.label: Only schemas with the exact br_<name>__ prefix are dropped
rubric.ruleStatement: drop_branch drops a schema only if Python `name.startswith(drop_prefix(br_name))` is true, using quoted identifiers, so stage schemas and other branches' schemas, including br_<name>x__ and br_<name>_other__, are never touched. 10 = tests include adversarial neighbours (br_feat2__analytics, br_fea__analytics, a schema containing '%' or '_' wildcard lookalikes) on real Warehouses; 8 = raw_shop, analytics, adops and br_other__ asserted untouched.
passCriteria: Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/application/test_drop_branch.py tests/unit/infrastructure/test_warehouse_schemas.py tests/unit/interface/test_drop_branch_command.py -q` with ADOPS_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN set: they pass with no skips.

On DuckDB and Postgres, a test creates raw_shop, analytics, adops, br_feat__raw_shop, br_feat__raw_shop_staging, br_feat__analytics, br_feat2__analytics and br_other__adops, runs drop-branch feat, and asserts exactly the three br_feat__ schemas are gone.
`grep -nEi "LIKE" src/adops/infrastructure/warehouse_schemas.py src/adops/application/drop_branch.py` prints nothing.
`grep -n 'DROP SCHEMA' src/adops/infrastructure/warehouse_schemas.py` shows the name wrapped in double quotes.
failureExamples: Listing uses `WHERE schema_name LIKE 'br_feat__%'`, where '_' is a wildcard, so 'br_feat2_analytics' or 'br_featx_analytics' also matches.
The prefix is computed from the raw branch argument rather than branch_environment_name, so 'Feat/X' drops nothing while its schemas remain.
Prefix 'br_feat' without the trailing '__' drops br_feat2__analytics.

rubric.label: Only .adops/dlt/br_<name> is removed locally
rubric.ruleStatement: The command deletes exactly local_state_dir(project, br_name) when it exists and never .adops/, another branch's state, stage's state or the DuckDB Warehouse file. 10 = a test also guards a branch name whose sanitized form could be empty or traverse paths; 8 = sibling dirs and the DuckDB file asserted present after the drop.
passCriteria: A test creates .adops/dlt/br_feat, .adops/dlt/br_feat2, .adops/dlt/stage and the DuckDB warehouse file, runs drop-branch feat, and asserts only .adops/dlt/br_feat is gone.
A test with no .adops/dlt/br_feat directory asserts the command succeeds.
`grep -n 'rmtree' src/adops/infrastructure/warehouse_schemas.py` shows it applied only to the local_state_dir result.
failureExamples: rmtree(local_state_dir(project, '')) when sanitizing yields '' deletes all of .adops/dlt.
The state folder is deleted before schemas are dropped, so a Warehouse failure leaves orphan schemas with no local state to re-run incrementally.

rubric.label: Repeated drops succeed and only stage's secret is resolved
rubric.ruleStatement: Running drop-branch twice, or for a branch that never existed, exits 0 with a plain message; it resolves only the stage Environment's Warehouse secret, so missing prod or dev secrets do not block it. 10 = a test leaves prod/dev secrets unset and asserts success; 8 = idempotency asserted on both Warehouse kinds.
passCriteria: A CliRunner test runs `adops drop-branch feat` twice against the same Warehouse and asserts exit code 0 both times.
A test with only the stage secret env var set (dev/prod secrets unset) asserts drop-branch succeeds.
`adops drop-branch '///'` exits non-zero with the PipelineValidationError usage message and drops nothing.
failureExamples: The command resolves all Environments' secrets up front and fails when prod's secret is absent on a developer laptop.
DROP SCHEMA without IF EXISTS raises when a concurrent drop already removed the staging schema.

rubric.label: Use case is Warehouse-agnostic and CLI errors leak nothing
rubric.ruleStatement: application/drop_branch.py decides which schemas to drop through the WarehouseSchemas Protocol and holds no SQL or path code; the CLI maps every failure via the accept_schema_command except ladder so no DSN or driver text is printed. 10 = the secret-absence assertion covers unreachable Warehouse, locked DuckDB and unexpected exceptions; 8 = covers unreachable Warehouse.
passCriteria: `grep -nE "SELECT|DROP|information_schema|rmtree|Path\(" src/adops/application/drop_branch.py` prints nothing.
A CliRunner test with an unreachable Postgres DSN containing a distinctive password asserts a non-zero exit and that the password is not in the output.
A test with a DuckDB file held by another process asserts a plain locked-Warehouse message and non-zero exit.
failureExamples: The use case filters with a SQL LIKE string it passes to the adapter, moving the destructive match logic out of tested Python.
A new except branch prints `str(exc)` for duckdb.IOException, which includes the file path and lock holder PID.

phases.healerHint: The likely failure is a SQL LIKE or missing trailing '__' that lets a neighbouring branch or *_staging schema slip through; fix by listing all schemas and filtering in Python with name.startswith(drop_prefix(branch_environment_name(branch, ...))), then quoting each name in DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS "..." CASCADE.

phases.name: Test branch defer and drop in demo E2E
phases.goal: Prove on both Postgres and DuckDB Warehouses in the Docker demo that a stage run saves fingerprints, a dbt-only change rebuilds only Transform and Reverse Sync without re-syncing, a Sync change re-syncs into br_ schemas, a no-change branch run defers everything, and drop-branch removes the br_ schemas while stage's stay. Record the schema-layout decision alongside.
phases.rationale: Unit tests use fakes or single adapters, so only the end-to-end demo shows the pieces agree on real dlt, dbt and Dagster with real schema names. The user requires each horizon to end with the Docker demo E2E proving the feature on both Warehouse kinds. ADR-0006 still describes a single env_<branch> schema dropped by CI. That wording must be clarified in the same change, so the docs match the code.
changes: Add test_branch_environment_* to tests/e2e/test_demo_sync.py, parametrized by the existing demo fixture over postgres and duckdb. Run `adops run shop_sync --env stage`, then edit dbt/models/customer_stats.sql and run --branch feat: assert the Sync Step is 'deferred to stage', br_feat__analytics exists, and no br_feat__raw_shop exists.

Edit pipelines/shop_sync.yaml's Sync Step and run --branch feat again: assert br_feat__raw_shop now holds rows. Revert both edits and run --branch feat2: assert every Step is deferred and the exit code is 0. Assert the Reverse Sync printed a Preview and the shop target is unchanged.

Run `adops drop-branch feat`: assert no br_feat__ schema remains (including *_staging) and that stage's raw_shop, analytics and adops tables are unchanged versus a snapshot taken before the branch runs. Compare before and after rather than absolute values, because the Postgres stage database persists across tests.

Change the known flaky ORPHAN_CUSTOMER_ID '999' assertion only if it stays a one-line change (match the Reverse Sync preview lines, not Dagster run UUIDs); otherwise leave it and record it as a known issue. Record the new E2E wall-clock time.

As steps in this phase: amend ADR-0006 with a clarifying note (per-kind br_<branch>__<schema> layout, manual drop-branch, '__' kept by disabling dlt dataset-name normalization, and the adops_raw_schema_<source> dbt-variable convention user dbt projects need for branch re-syncs). Add Step Fingerprint, Changed Step, Defer, Branch Schema and Drop to GLOSSARY.md, and reword 'deleted when merged or closed'. Log the decision and the accept-schema --branch known gap in decisions.md.
phases.expectedResult: tests/e2e/test_demo_sync.py::test_branch_environment passes for both postgres and duckdb in the CI e2e job within its 20-minute limit.
guardNotes: g5: the new scenario adds about 5 adops runs per Warehouse kind on top of the ~110s baseline, well inside the 20-minute timeout. The test runs stage itself and never assumes an empty stage.
g9: the test edits files only in the scaffolded tmp project, not in src/adops/templates/demo, so DEMO_FILES is unchanged.

rubric.label: Demo proves defer, rebuild-only-changed and re-sync-on-Sync-change on Postgres and DuckDB
rubric.ruleStatement: Vision success criterion (5): Branch Environments are per-branch schemas in the stage Warehouse that defer to stage, rebuild only changed Steps + dependents, re-sync only when a Sync Step changed. The E2E proves this on both Warehouse kinds: a dbt-only edit defers the Sync and creates br_feat__analytics without br_feat__raw_shop; a Sync edit creates br_feat__raw_shop with rows; a reverted project defers every Step and exits 0. 10 = also asserts the Changed-Step rebuild output names each rebuilt Step; 8 = the three scenarios asserted on both kinds.
passCriteria: Run `uv run pytest tests/e2e -m e2e -k branch_environment -v`: both the postgres and duckdb parametrizations pass.
The test asserts the output of the dbt-only branch run contains the Sync Step with 'deferred to stage', and that information_schema has br_feat__analytics and no br_feat__raw_shop.
After the Sync edit, the test asserts `SELECT count(*) FROM br_feat__raw_shop.<table>` is > 0.
The reverted-project branch run asserts exit code 0 and every Step reported as deferred.

The test assumes an empty stage and asserts absolute row counts that fail on the persistent Postgres stage database.

rubric.label: Stage tables, fingerprints, snapshots and the shop target are unchanged by branch runs and the drop
rubric.ruleStatement: Stage tables, fingerprints and snapshots unchanged by any branch run or drop, and the branch Reverse Sync only previews. The E2E snapshots stage's raw_shop, analytics, adops tables (including _adops_step_fingerprints and schema snapshots) and the shop target before branch runs and asserts equality afterwards. 10 = comparison covers row contents (hash or full select), not just counts; 8 = row counts plus fingerprint rows compared.
passCriteria: The test captures, before the first --branch run, the rows of adops._adops_step_fingerprints, the schema-snapshot table and per-table row counts of raw_shop and analytics, and asserts they are equal after `adops drop-branch feat`.
The test asserts the branch run output contains a Reverse Sync Preview line and the shop target table's rows are unchanged.
The orphan-customer/preview assertion matches Reverse Sync Preview lines, not Dagster run UUIDs.
failureExamples: The comparison happens after the stage run but before the drop, missing a drop that removed stage's adops_staging schema.

successCriteria: Done when ALL hold. (1) A successful stage run of a Step, after all its Checks pass, saves that Step's Step Fingerprint in the stage Warehouse's adops schema. The fingerprint is a deterministic hash of the Step's YAML definition plus the files it depends on (for a Transform Step, the dbt project files, excluding generated target/, logs/ and .adops/). Running the same files on another machine or another day gives the same hash. dev runs and Branch Environment runs never write stage fingerprints. (2) `adops run <pipeline> --branch <name>` derives a Branch Environment from the stage Environment's settings: same Warehouse, Sources and targets. It names it br_<sanitized name> and uses schemas br_<name>__raw_<source>, br_<name>__analytics and br_<name>__adops. It computes fingerprints for every Step. The first Step whose fingerprint differs from stage's, or that stage has none for, and every later Step run in branch schemas. Earlier Steps do not run, and the Steps that do run read stage's raw_<source>/analytics tables for them. A Transform Step after an unchanged Sync Step reads stage's raw_<source>. A Reverse Sync Step reads the branch's analytics when the Transform was rebuilt, and stage's otherwise. (3) A branch run re-syncs Sources only when a Sync Step, or a Step before it, changed. (4) A branch run where nothing changed runs no Step, exits 0 and says it uses stage. A branch run with no stage fingerprints for the Pipeline fails with a clear, sanitized error asking you to run stage first. --branch without a stage Environment in adops.yaml fails clearly. (5) Every Reverse Sync in a Branch Environment yields a Preview and never writes, enforced by the existing exact stage/prod name rule. (6) The drop command removes every Warehouse schema with prefix br_<name>__ (CASCADE) and the local dlt state folder <project>/.adops/dlt/<branch env>. It never touches a schema without that exact prefix, uses quoted identifiers, and succeeds idempotently when nothing exists. (7) Stage tables, fingerprints and snapshots are byte-for-byte unchanged by any branch run or drop. (8) The Docker demo E2E, on both Postgres and DuckDB Warehouses: runs stage; changes only the dbt model and shows the branch rebuilds only Transform + Reverse Sync with no re-sync; changes the Sync Step and shows a re-sync into br_ schemas; shows a no-change branch run; drops the branch and asserts the br_ schemas are gone and stage's remain. The whole E2E finishes inside the unchanged 20-minute CI job. (9) The repo gates hold: 100% line+branch coverage with no new pragma; domain/application purity rules; no secret value in any output, log or error (asserted by tests); `uv sync --locked`; wheel template check. (10) ADR-0006's schema wording is clarified by a recorded decision (env_<branch> → per-kind br_<branch>__<schema>), and GLOSSARY gains the new terms.
